geology_notes: Churchill Resources holds the Foxtrot past-producing antimony mine (Frost Cove / Black Raven property) in central Newfoundland, and has expanded its district land position through the March 2026 Golden Baie option (39,925 ha, TSXV-approved March 27, 2026) and a Black Raven LOI. Confirmed geological highlights from accessible disclosures: (1) FC25-27: 13.00% Sb over 0.57m at Frost Cove — validated after the May 2026 data-correction release that downgraded the broader initial assay dataset; (2) a second new polymetallic system at southern Frost Cove / Black Raven yielding 7.25% Sb over 1.98m; (3) a 20-vein Au-Ag-Mo-Pb-Zn swarm at Pomley Cove Pond with surface channel results including 17.3 g/t Au and 130 g/t Ag; (4) zinc grab samples at Black Raven reaching 5.25%, 11.03%, and 12.11% Zn with associated Au, Ag, and Pb. Nine 2026 drill holes completed circa July 13 remain without confirmed public assay release as of July 28 — now fifteen days since the 'imminent' assay announcement, and no results headline has appeared in accessible news indices. The August 2023 NI 43-101 technical report remains the most recent on file; its first 60 pages yielded no compliant resource estimate. All five resource/reserve fields are null per extraction. Score of 3 reflects confirmed high-grade multi-commodity mineralisation across a consolidated NL property package, constrained by absence of a compliant resource estimate and the still-pending 2026 assay results.

catalyst_notes: Macro catalyst: China's September 2024 antimony export controls restricted supply from the dominant global producer and have sustained government urgency across Canada, the US, the EU, and Australia for domestic and allied critical mineral supply chains. Antimony is named in Canada's Critical Minerals Strategy and on the US Defense Production Act designated minerals list, making Foxtrot a credible candidate for NRCan/provincial grant support and strategic partnership interest. This macro tailwind remains durable as of July 28, 2026. Company-specific catalyst (adverse development confirmed): CRI shares fell approximately 20% on July 15, 2026, closing near C$0.04. The specific trigger for the decline was not independently confirmable (the linked financial-news article returned HTTP 403), but the timing — two days after the nine 2026 drill holes were reported as completed circa July 13 and while assay results remained pending — is notable. The 2026 assay batch remains without confirmed public release as of July 28, now fifteen days since the 'imminent' announcement and no results headline has appeared in accessible search indices. A 20% intraday decline at $0.04 implies roughly a C$12.7M market cap and may reduce the company's ability to attract a future equity financing on favourable terms. Score reduced from 3 to 2: the macro tailwind remains intact but the unexplained July 15 stock decline raises the possibility of an adverse company-specific development, and fifteen days of silence past an 'imminent' assay promise erodes near-term catalyst timing confidence.

Nine 2026 drill holes completed circa July 13 remain without confirmed public assay release as of July 28 — fifteen days since the 'imminent' announcement; no results headline has appeared in accessible search indices. A new adverse data point: CRI shares fell approximately 20% on July 15, 2026, closing near C$0.04 (implied market cap roughly C$12.7M at 316.7M shares issued); the specific cause was not confirmable from accessible sources but the timing is suspicious. Cap table per the April 2026 MD&A extraction: 316,681,940 shares issued and outstanding; 342,756,940 fully diluted (2,625,000 warrants + 23,450,000 options — strike prices and expiry dates unextracted). No NI 43-101 compliant resource estimate is on file; all resource/reserve fields remain null. Catalyst score reduced to 2 to reflect the unexplained July 15 stock decline and the prolonged delay past the 'imminent' assay announcement. Maintain WATCH at low confidence: the critical-minerals strategic positioning with confirmed high-grade results justifies continued monitoring, but the July 15 price event and fifteen-day assay delay are near-term negative signals that prevent upgrading conviction.
